facts.text: The node includes the gym_env RegisterSpaces, SensorMessage, ActuatorMessage, CloseEnv, ResetEnv, StepEnv and GetReward headers together with the webots_ros get_bool, get_float, set_int, set_float and Float64Stamped headers.
MOTOR_NUMBER is 9.
The motor_names array names the seven Panda arm joints and the two finger joints in the order panda_joint1 through panda_joint7 followed by panda_finger_joint1 and panda_finger_joint2.
sensorCallback stores each Float64Stamped value in sensor_values and publishes a SensorMessage carrying all nine values.

initSensors calls each <model>/<joint>_sensor/enable service with value 80 and, when the call succeeds, subscribes to that sensor's Float64Stamped value topic and busy-waits until the subscription has a publisher.
sensorSpacesCallback returns motorMin-2e-5 as low, motorMax+2e-5 as high and the topic /joint_sensors/value.
actuatorSpacesCallback returns a nine-element action space with low -1.0 and high 1.0 and the topic /joint_actuators/value.
actuatorCommandCallback adds motorRange[i]*actions[i]/20 to each setpoint, clamps the setpoint to [motorMin[i], motorMax[i]] and calls the joint set_position service.
initActuators reads each joint's get_max_position and get_min_position, stores max-1e-5 and min+1e-5, and computes range as max-min.
stepCallback calls the stepEnv client with no retry limit until a call succeeds with response.success, and then returns true.

resetCallback returns false unless the resetEnv get_bool call succeeds with value true; it then calls stepEnv with value 8 once, ignoring the result, calls it again until one call succeeds, sleeping 0.5 s after each failure, calls initSensors and returns true.
closeCallback logs Close and returns true without calling any device method.
rewardCallback computes the negative sum over the nine joints of the distance from each joint position to the middle of its range and returns it in response.reward.
main creates the reset client on <model>/supervisor/simulation_reset and the step client on <model>/robot/time_step, and sets the step request value to 80 ms.
The node advertises /joint_sensors, /joint_actuators, /webots/step, /webots/close, /webots/reset and /reward.
The node subscribes /joint_actuators/value and advertises /joint_sensors/value.
main subscribes /joint_actuators/value with a queue size of 1, advertises /joint_sensors/value with a queue size of 1 and then calls ros::spin().
The launch file includes webots_ros webots.launch in realtime mode with the panda.wbt world and starts the gym_env_webots_node executable.
The Panda world fixes basicTimeStep to 8 ms and instantiates the Panda robot with controller "ros".
The Panda robot runs the ros controller with the --synchronize controller argument and supervisor TRUE.
The Panda PROTO declares synchronization with the default TRUE.
motorSetPoints is a global array initialised to zero.
The Panda PROTO declares panda_finger_joint1 as a LinearMotor with maxPosition 0.04.
The Panda PROTO declares panda_finger_joint2 as a LinearMotor with maxPosition 0.04.
package.xml declares build/exec dependencies on gym_env, roscpp, std_msgs and webots_ros.

determinism.notes: Canned service replies and an analytic setpoint model; no Webots engine, Panda physics, joint controller, contact, sensor, clock or wall-clock pacing, and no trajectory replay

fidelity.engine: analytic:ROS-free fake of the node's setpoint arithmetic (no Webots physics)
gaps: the fake is a ROS-free transport: it answers the declared endpoints from placeholder state and runs no Webots engine, Panda model, joint controller, contacts, sensors or pacing

an action publication updates the fake's copy of the node's setpoints exactly as actuatorCommandCallback does (motorRange*action/20, clamped to the joint range); the joint limits are placeholders copied from the Panda PROTO (finger minimum 0, not stated), not values read through get_min_position/get_max_position

a fake /webots/step moves every fake joint to its last set_position target in one step; real Webots joints move under their motor velocity and force limits over many 8 ms steps, so a real observation after one 80 ms step need not equal the setpoint

a fake /joint_sensors/value subscription answers at once; whether the live node publishes a sample after a step's reply depends on the webots_ros controller (outside the clone), and the act-and-step receipt is unknown when none arrives within its 2 s observation bound

the fake applies an action publication before it answers the next step (unless its action_after_step switch is set); live, rosbridge forwards the publication and the /webots/step call over different ROS connections and the node serves both from ros::spin() (253, 258, 265), so the step may run before actuatorCommandCallback, and the first action after rosbridge advertises /joint_actuators/value may be lost before the node's subscription connects: a completed act-and-step receipt's observation need not reflect the action
the /webots/step and /webots/reset replies are immediate; the upstream calls the Webots robot/time_step client and the supervisor simulation_reset client, which the fake does not model

model review: resetCallback retries its time_step call every 0.5 s and initSensors busy-waits for publishers without a bound (171-195, 65-79), so a reset can outlast the 2 s default binding timeout and the e-stop then reports SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED; motorSetPoints (31, 117-125) survives the reset, so the first action after it jumps back toward the pre-reset setpoints
the upstream basicTimeStep is 8 ms and the node requests an 80 ms step; the fake has no physics timestep and runs no wall-clock loop
the upstream /reward callback uses cached sensor_values and does not itself step the simulation; the fake returns a fixed placeholder reward
/joint_sensors and /joint_actuators RegisterSpaces calls, /webots/close, the model_name topic, the external gym_env package and ROS namespace remapping are outside this package's declared surface
no Webots engine, ROS graph, rosbridge deployment or hardware was contacted by this package; the only evidence is the fake backend

safe_state.description: The safe-state action is the fixed /webots/reset service: its reply acknowledges that the Webots supervisor accepted simulation_reset and that a later 8 ms time_step succeeded (at least two run). The Panda's ros controller runs with --synchronize, the configuration in which the world advances only on time_step calls; MHS sends none after the latch, but other ROS clients are not fenced. motorSetPoints is not cleared, and what Webots restores is outside the clone.
